en.purpose: To derive the FIGO 2013 stage and substage for ovarian, fallopian tube, and primary peritoneal carcinoma based on recorded staging-relevant findings.
en.use:
Use to assign FIGO 2013 stage (IA-IVB) for ovarian carcinoma, fallopian tube carcinoma, and primary peritoneal carcinoma based on structured staging findings.

Inputs processed
- Primary peritoneal carcinoma (yes/no)
- Tumour confined to ovaries/ovary or fallopian tube(s) (yes/no)
- Pelvic extension below pelvic brim (yes/no)
- Extrapelvic peritoneal spread (yes/no)
- Retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis (yes/no)
- Distant metastasis excluding peritoneal metastasis (yes/no)
- Ovary and fallopian tube involvement pattern (laterality / confinement category)
- Tumour spill / surface / cytology finding (none vs IC1/IC2/IC3 features)
- Pelvic extension pattern (uterus/adnexa vs other pelvic tissues)
- Largest retroperitoneal nodal metastasis size (≤10 mm vs >10 mm)
- Extrapelvic peritoneal disease extent (microscopic vs ≤2 cm vs >2 cm)
- Type of distant metastasis (pleural cytology vs parenchymal/extra-abdominal)

Staging logic
- If distant metastasis is present → Stage IV (IVA or IVB depending on type).
- Else if extrapelvic peritoneal disease and/or retroperitoneal lymph node metastasis is present → Stage III (substage depends on peritoneal extent and nodal size).
- Else if pelvic extension is present (or primary peritoneal carcinoma with pelvic-only disease) → Stage II (IIA/IIB depends on pelvic extension pattern).
- Else if disease is confined to ovaries/tubes → Stage I (IA/IB/IC1-IC3 depends on laterality and spill/surface/cytology).
en.misuse:
Not to be used for clinical or pathological TNM staging.
Not to be used for staging of other gynaecological malignancies.
